decisions.reason: The web tool is tightly aligned with the firm's engineering-planner customer base, likely cheap to maintain, and still worth keeping open as a low-cost option even after two years.

The fouling detection system is more demanding to support than a simple tool, but it fits the firm's efficiency and digital-monitoring direction and there is still not enough negative evidence to justify abandonment.

The spring-controlled flap weir is close to the established hydraulic offering, so for an expanding firm it is sensible to keep this very new adjacent product on the market while demand becomes clearer.

The energy management system matches the firm's strategic move toward networked, efficient infrastructure operations, and despite some likely support cost it is too new and too central to future positioning to drop now.

The overflow flap gate line sits close to the core business, benefits from the firm's project and service capabilities, and its dedicated presentation suggests enough commitment to continue while the market response develops.
